article.headline: UK Braces for Hottest May Day on Record as 30C Heat Continues
article.summary: The UK is expected to experience its hottest May day on record on Monday, with temperatures forecast to reach as high as 34C, breaking the previous May record of 32.8C set over 80 years ago. Eight regions in southern and eastern England have officially entered heatwave conditions, and amber heat health alerts are in place in parts of the Midlands and eastern England. The hot weather is expected to continue throughout the week, with temperatures potentially reaching the mid-30s in southern Britain.
article.body:
According to the Met Office, the 32.3C recorded at Kew Gardens in south-west London on Sunday was the highest of the year so far. The heatwave conditions were met in several parts of the UK on Sunday, after three days at or above the temperature threshold. The BBC's meteorologist, Tomasz Schafernaker, stated that Monday and Tuesday are forecast to be the hottest days of the week, with temperatures on both days reaching the mid-30s in southern Britain. Monday is expected to bring the most widespread heat, with all nations set for their hottest weather so far this year.

The heatwave is not limited to daytime temperatures, as it is possible that somewhere in the UK will stay warmer than the May record of 18.9C set in Folkestone in 1947 on Monday or Tuesday night. Wales could also set a new May heat record in the next few days, surpassing the 30.6C recorded in Newport in 1944. The hot weather may spark a few thunderstorms in central England and Wales on Tuesday, but they are likely to be very localized and not enough to cause a significant break from the heat.

The heatwave is consistent with what would be expected in a changing, hotter climate, according to the latest European State of the Climate report. Europe is the fastest warming continent in the world, with heatwaves becoming more frequent and more intense. The UK experiences its highest temperatures at the end of July or the beginning of August, so it's likely that even higher temperatures will be seen during the summer.

A break in the heat is expected widely across much of eastern and southeastern England on Wednesday, as cooler air temporarily spreads off the North Sea. However, Wales and southwestern England will remain fairly hot, sheltered from the North Sea breeze. By Thursday, the supply of cooler air will be cut off as hot air resurges from France once again, leading to temperatures increasing, with 30C back on the cards.

The jet stream, which is currently to the north of the UK, will wobble back southwards next weekend, bringing areas of low pressure, occasional rain, stronger winds, and a drop in temperature as the UK heads into the first week of June. This will provide some respite from the heatwave, but it's likely that the UK will experience even higher temperatures during the summer.
article.takeaway: The UK is expected to experience its hottest May day on record on Monday, with temperatures forecast to reach as high as 34C, breaking the previous May record of 32.8C set over 80 years ago.
